intended_object: The component on one open U of the "right-order" base-change map: for a morphism h : M → N of presheaves of A-modules, it is the map h_U ⊗ id : M(U) ⊗_{A(U)} B(U) → N(U) ⊗_{A(U)} B(U). I inferred this from the docstring and from the lemma `rightSectionMap_pure`.
explanation: This is an internal helper. The library has two versions of sectionwise tensoring, B(U) ⊗ M(U) and M(U) ⊗ B(U). `rightSectionMap` moves the existing map `tensorSectionMap` over to the right-order version: it applies the comparison isomorphism `rightSectionIso` for M, then `tensorSectionMap`, then the inverse isomorphism for N. Its only purpose is to give the components of `rightPresheafMap` and to state the lemmas `rightSectionMap_pure` and `rightPresheafMap_restriction`. It is not a separate notion from the literature. Mathematically it is just extension of scalars applied to h_U, and the "right order" choice is a detail of how the library is built. The construction is correct: `rightSectionMap_pure` shows it sends m ⊗ b to h(m) ⊗ b. Still, it is bookkeeping for the symmetry argument, not a definition of a mathematical object in its own right.
